clue.text: Genius of story books

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone praising the brilliance on show in a collection of stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural gift or flair is a synonym for genius in the sense of outstanding ability.

clue.text: One who buys key American book by King

parts.note: C is a musical key
a tome is a large book
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a novel by Stephen King, perhaps an American edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper or client who purchases goods is what a shop calls its buyer.

clue.text: Study follows paperback's plot

indicators.note: follows puts the study after the paper's letters in the answer

parts.note: a rag is slang for a newspaper, and 'back' turns those letters around, giving the paper read backwards
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A reader finds the plot of a paperback in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paperback' is one word but splits as paper (RAG) and back, turning it into GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of ground cultivated with flowers or vegetables is a garden.

clue.text: Continuations of story speak of search for sources of water

indicators.note: speak of tells us to say the phrase out loud and listen to its sound

parts.note: to search for sources of water is to seek wells

explanation.surface: A story's follow-ups apparently talk about prospecting for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Follow-on books or films continuing an earlier tale are its sequels.

clue.text: Book about gravity's reach in translation

indicators.note: a translation recasts its text, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: A book about the far-reaching effects of gravity, read in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a suspect is to formally accuse them, the police sense of the verb.

clue.text: 'Mystery novel' in quotes

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: The phrase 'mystery novel' appears in quotation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsolved puzzle or open query is a mystery; both are things not yet answered.

clue.text: Despondent about you in France, stuck with tariff and unable to take any more

indicators.note: about means the first word wraps around the others

parts.note: despondent means sad

indicators.note: stuck with joins the next piece on after the French word

parts.note: tu is French for you
a tariff is a rate charged

explanation.surface: A gloomy Frenchman hit with a tariff can bear no more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaked through can absorb nothing further, so it is full to capacity.

clue.text: Call round

definitions.meaning: to call is to cry out loudly
in Britain, a round of drinks you pay for is 'your ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A loud cry is a call; buying the drinks in a pub is, in British slang, one's turn to pay.

clue.text: Sang loudly with band, due to being drunk

parts.note: a belt is a band worn round the waist

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer bellowed along with the band because they were tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a song with great volume is the idiom for singing loudly.

clue.text: Type of writing of period seen regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter from these words

explanation.surface: A style of writing typical of a particular era.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary written language not in verse is one broad kind of writing.

clue.text: Vegetable in book? Radish?

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which vegetable appears in a book: a radish?
explanation.definitionFit: The green pods also called ladies' fingers are a vegetable.

clue.text: Note my oddly original word

indicators.note: oddly means arranged in a strange way, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone asks us to note a strange original word of theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: The root form from which a later word derives is its source word, in linguistics.

clue.text: To want not a cent? Weird this is in both the US and Canada

definitions.text: this is in both the US and Canada

indicators.note: not means the following item is excluded

parts.note: to want is to lack
C is the abbreviation for a cent
weird means eerie

explanation.surface: Someone penniless finds it strange to be on both sides of a border.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Great Lakes straddles the boundary between the two countries.

clue.text: Top pieces of literature in bookcases, recording and retelling yarns

definitions.text: Top pieces of literature in bookcases, recording and retelling yarns

indicators.note: the top piece of each word is its first letter

parts.words: literature in bookcases, recording and retelling yarns

explanation.surface: The best of literature sits on shelves, preserving and retelling stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of books on shelves, storing written stories, describes a lending or reference collection.

clue.text: She jointly made Columbus sail and able to roam

indicators.note: to roam is to wander, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A queen backed Columbus, letting him set sail and roam.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Isabella of Castile, with Ferdinand of Aragon, funded Columbus's voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish queen who, together with her husband, sponsored Columbus's voyage made his name.

clue.text: Learn from a book: note, a hardback

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
the back of the word hard is its last letter

explanation.surface: Studying a book: one takes note of a hardback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hardback' splits into hard and back, the back of 'hard' being D.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in words on a page is how one learns from a text.

clue.text: Habitat of Tasmanian devil, evolving with limited parts lost

indicators.note: evolving means changing form, so the letters are rearranged once the others are lost

explanation.surface: A Tasmanian devil adapts to a habitat where it has lost some limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of 'limited' from TASMANIAN DEVIL ('parts lost') and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical grassland is the home environment of many animals.

clue.text: Stories in books

definitions.meaning: a firm's financial records, kept in ledgers

explanation.definitionFit: Reports of events are tales; a company's ledgers are its financial records.

clue.text: Passage from a booklet

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex libris
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: A passage taken out of a small pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A short section quoted from a text is a passage.

clue.text: Capital writer, initially keen to meet aristocrat, loses head and gets kiss after a month

indicators.note: after places the kiss behind the month
initially means take the first letter
loses head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an earl is an aristocrat
Mar is short for March

explanation.surface: A keen writer meets a nobleman, loses his head and kisses someone in March.
explanation.definitionFit: The German philosopher wrote Das Kapital, a critique of capitalism.

clue.text: Opposed to opening, dropping, opening, dropping?

indicators.note: these words tell us to shed the first letter of the word for shutting

parts.note: the opposite of opening is closing

explanation.surface: A riddle of repeated words about opening and dropping.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding or letting go of something is losing it.

clue.text: Potentially constituent narrative ultimately lost for reader

indicators.note: lost means the letter is removed

parts.note: an elector may become a constituent of an MP

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter

explanation.surface: A would-be voter loses the end of a story while reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reads lessons aloud in church is a reader.

clue.text: Old story offers a clue to boot

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the end of a leg is where a boot goes; also a map key gives clues

explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' looks like 'as well'; it is where a boot sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth handed down is a traditional tale; split, the word names where a leg ends.

clue.text: Epistolary novel: badly written letters in yarns? I opt out (this was pre-GCSE)

indicators.note: badly written means the letters are jumbled, once those of the others go out

explanation.surface: Writing a novel in letters badly earned poor marks in an old exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of 'yarns I opt' from EPISTOLARY NOVEL ('out') and rearrange. O level was the British school exam replaced by GCSE in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary-level exam for British sixteen-year-olds preceded the current qualification.

clue.text: Old penny dreadful seen as impenetrable

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for a pre-decimal British penny

indicators.note: dreadful means awful, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A cheap Victorian thriller, a penny dreadful, is found impossible to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: A penny dreadful was a cheap sensational Victorian serial.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick and hard to get through, physically or mentally, is the sense shared.

clue.text: One has bras etc in drawer!

parts.note: split as DRAW + ER: drag means draw and the Queen is ER

explanation.surface: A chest of drawers holds lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture; DRAW-ER is drag plus ER, the Queen. A man in women's clothing has bras.
explanation.definitionFit: A male performer in women's clothing would wear bras and similar.

clue.text: Stir up novel so it ends in twist

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a bend is a twist or turn

indicators.note: the way the word ends is its last letter

explanation.surface: A novel stirs things up so that it ends with a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix ingredients together is to combine them by stirring.

clue.text: Cutlet of muscle core, chopped thin, zebra's head and veal, even

indicators.note: the core is the middle letters
chopped means cut up, so the letters are mixed
the head is the first letter
even means the even-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A recipe: a cutlet of muscle, chopped thin, with zebra and veal.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaded Austrian escalope of veal is a thin fried cut of meat.
